questions.q: Why would an admin build a custom object like Energy Audit?
options: Because custom objects run faster than standard objects
Because standard objects cannot hold any records
Because no standard object represents that specific kind of data
Because custom objects don't require fields
questions.explain: Custom objects exist to cover data that no standard object (Account, Contact, Lead, etc.) represents.

questions.q: Once a custom object is created, how does it behave compared to a standard object?
options: It cannot have relationships to other objects
It can never appear in a report
It cannot have a page layout
It behaves the same way — fields, records, relationships, and reports all work identically
questions.explain: A custom object gets the same baseline capabilities as a standard object once it's created: fields, records, relationships, and reporting all work the same way.

questions.q: Where do you go to create a new custom object?
options: The Reports tab
Object Manager's Create button
The Chatter feed
A Quote record's actions menu
questions.explain: Object Manager's Create button offers Custom Object (and Custom Object from Spreadsheet) as the starting points for building one.

questions.q: Looking only at a record's page, with no access to Object Manager, how easy is it to tell a custom object's record from a standard object's record?
options: Often not obvious at all — the header, tabs, and layout look the same either way
Impossible to confuse — custom object records are always a different color
Custom object records never have a Related tab
Standard object records are always read-only
questions.explain: Custom and standard object records can look nearly identical on the page — same header style, same Details/Related tabs — which is exactly the point of the comparison in this lesson.

questions.q: What is one real, structural difference between a custom object and a standard object?
options: A custom object can never have fields
A custom object's API name ends in __c
A custom object cannot be reported on
A custom object has no owner field
questions.explain: A custom object's API name always ends in __c, and (unlike most standard objects) it can be deleted — those are real structural differences, even though the two behave the same day to day.
